```{r setup, include=FALSE}
knitr::opts_chunk$set(echo = TRUE)
```

necessary libraries.
```{r}
library(dplyr)
library(ggplot2)
library(tidyverse)
library(openxlsx)
library(stringdist)
library(maps)
library(zipcodeR)
```

reading in file. A dataframe is created representing the 1975 spreadsheet
```{r}
grants1975 = read.csv("grant1975.csv", header = TRUE)
```

adding columns based on known info. ID is row number, and we separate source file to create the columns year and month. 
```{r}
grants1975 <- grants1975 %>%
  mutate(ID = row_number(), .before = 1)

grants1975 <- grants1975 %>%
  separate(source_file,
           into = c("year", "month_num", "month"),
           sep = "-") %>%
   mutate(
    month = month.name[match(month, month.abb)]
  ) %>%
  select(ID, year, month, everything(), -month_num)
```

We noticed that many rows are duplicates of previous ones. we remove the duplicates here
```{r}
length(unique(grants1975$grant.number))
grants1975 = grants1975[!duplicated(grants1975$grant.number), ]
```

grant type is either continuation, new, or blank. will fix below using fuzzy matching, a string matching method that assigns a score or distance to an entry on how similar it is to the keywords its analyzing. here, the keywords would be the entries in valid_types. Based on the distance from each entry to a keyword, we either will or will not assign that entry to the keyword. my algorithm used is below
```{r}
sum(is.na(grants1975$grant.type))
table(grants1975$grant.type)
```

```{r}
grants1975$grant.type[trimws(grants1975$grant.type) == ""] = "X"
valid_types <- c(
  "NEW",
  "CONTINUATION",
  "X"
)

grants1975$grant.type_clean <- valid_types[
  amatch(grants1975$grant.type, valid_types, method = "jw", maxDist = 0.25)
]
grants1975$grant.type_clean[is.na(grants1975$grant.type_clean)] = paste0("incorrect_", grants1975$grant.type[is.na(grants1975$grant.type_clean)])
```

we can see our algorithms results in grant.type_clean, and the original column in grant.type
```{r}
grants1975[, c("grant.type", "grant.type_clean")]
```
our results are good, so we overwrite the old column with our new, cleaned column
```{r}
grants1975$grant.type = grants1975$grant.type_clean
grants1975 <- grants1975 %>% select(-c(grant.type_clean))
```

everything should be construction for program. will fix below
```{r}
sum(is.na(grants1975$program))
sort(table(grants1975$program), decreasing = TRUE)
```

```{r}
grants1975$program = ifelse(trimws(grants1975$program) == "", "X", "CONSTRUCTION")
```

```{r}
grants1975$step[trimws(grants1975$step) == ""] = "X"
```

Again, we use fuzzy matching to clean census.population. we follow an algorithm similar to the other algorithms we used for fuzzy matching
```{r}

```

```{r}
grants1975$census.population[trimws(grants1975$census.population) == ""] = "X"
valid_pops = c(
  "OVER 500,000",
  "LESS THAN 2,500",
  "2,500-5,000",
  "X",
  "5,001-25,000",
  "2,500-5,000",
  "25,001-50,000",
  "10,001-25,000",
  "50,001-125,000",
  "250,001-500,000",
  "125,001-250,000",
  "5,001-10,000"
)

grants1975$census.population_clean <- valid_pops[
  amatch(grants1975$census.population, valid_pops, method = "jw", maxDist = 0.25)
]

table(grants1975$census.population_clean, useNA = "always")
```
my new, cleaned values are in the census.population_clean column
```{r}
grants1975$census.population_clean[is.na(grants1975$census.population_clean)] = paste0("incorrect_", grants1975$census.population[is.na(grants1975$census.population_clean)])
```

For state, we used R's built-in character vector state.abb to match state abbreviations. We also add DC for good measure, PR for puerto rico, VI for virgin islands, and NB, which is what Nebraska was until a later date.
```{r}
sort(table(grants1975$state), decreasing = TRUE)
```

```{r}
states <- c(state.abb, "DC", "NB", "PR")
grants1975$state_clean <- toupper(trimws(as.character(grants1975$state)))

grants1975$state_clean <- grants1975$state_clean |>
  gsub("0", "O", x = _) |>
  gsub("1", "I", x = _) |>
  gsub("5", "S", x = _) |>
  gsub("8", "B", x = _) |>
  gsub("2", "Z", x = _) |>
  gsub("6", "G", x = _)
grants1975$state_clean <- sub(
  ".*\\b([A-Z]{2})\\b.*",
  "\\1",
  grants1975$state_clean
)

# Validate
grants1975$state_clean <- ifelse(
  grants1975$state_clean %in% states,
  grants1975$state_clean,
  NA
)
sort(table(grants1975$state_clean, useNA = "always"), decreasing = TRUE)
```

My new, cleaned column is state_clean
```{r}
grants1975$state_clean[is.na(grants1975$state_clean)] = paste0("incorrect_", grants1975$state[is.na(grants1975$state_clean)])
grants1975[, c("state", "state_clean")]
```

our cleaning was successful, so we override the old column with my new column
```{r}
grants1975$state = grants1975$state_clean
grants1975 = grants1975 %>% select(-c(state_clean))
```

Now we fix award date. i can notice some dates look to be incomplete. thus i am marking them as incomplete
```{r}
grants1975$award.date[trimws(grants1975$award.date) == ""] = "X"
```

```{r}
clean_date = function(x) {
  
  x = trimws(as.character(x))
  d = as.Date(x, format = "%m-%d-%y")
  return(d)
}
```

We get dates to all have a similar format and represent the correct date. anything that is ambiguous is flagged
```{r}
grants1975$award.date_clean = sapply(grants1975$award.date, clean_date)
grants1975$award.date_clean = as.Date(grants1975$award.date_clean, origin = "1970-01-01")
grants1975$award.date_clean = format(grants1975$award.date_clean, "%m-%d-%y")
sort(table(grants1975$award.date_clean, useNA = "always"), decreasing = TRUE)
grants1975$award.date_clean[is.na(grants1975$award.date_clean)] = paste0("incorrect_", grants1975$award.date[is.na(grants1975$award.date_clean)])
grants1975$award.date_clean[trimws(grants1975$award.date) == ""] = "X"
```

```{r}
grants1975[, c("award.date", "award.date_clean")]
```

our cleaning was successful, so we override the old column with my new column
```{r}
grants1975$award.date = grants1975$award.date_clean
grants1975 = grants1975 %>%  select(-c(award.date_clean))
```

for CD, we clean up the cells so that they are all numeric. random nonsense is removed. leading 0s are kept. CDs also only go up to 435, so numbers above that will be flagged
```{r}
clean_num = function(x) {
  
  x = as.character(x)
  x = gsub("[^0-9\\.]", "", x)
  as.numeric(x)
}
```

```{r}
grants1975$CD_clean = sapply(grants1975$CD, clean_num)
grants1975$CD_clean[trimws(grants1975$CD) == ""] = "X"
grants1975$CD_clean[is.na(grants1975$CD_clean)] = paste0("incorrect_", grants1975$CD[is.na(grants1975$CD_clean)])
x_num = suppressWarnings(as.numeric(grants1975$CD))
grants1975$CD_clean <- as.character(grants1975$CD)
grants1975$CD_clean[!is.na(x_num) & x_num > 435] <-
  paste0("incorrect_", grants1975$CD[!is.na(x_num) & x_num > 435])
grants1975[, c("CD", "CD_clean")]
```
We override the old column with my new column
```{r}
grants1975$CD = grants1975$CD_clean
grants1975 = grants1975 %>%  select(-c(CD_clean))
```

For region, we do something similar to CD. however, we also check if the number of characters is over 2. if it is, then the value is incorrect. usually these values were zipcodes
```{r}
clean_region = function(x) {
  
  x = as.character(x)
  reg = regmatches(x, regexpr("\\d+", x))
  if (length(reg) == 0 || reg == "") {
    return("X")
  }
  if (nchar(reg) > 2) {
    return("X")
  }
  return(as.numeric(reg))
}
```

```{r}
grants1975$region_clean = sapply(grants1975$region, clean_region)
sort(table(grants1975$region_clean, useNA = "always"), decreasing = TRUE)
```
my new, cleaned entries are below in region_clean
```{r}
grants1975[, c("region", "region_clean")]
```
our cleaning was successful, so we override the old column with my new column
```{r}
grants1975$region = grants1975$region_clean
grants1975 = grants1975 %>%  select(-c(region_clean))
```

From project period, we split the two dates to create two new columns: project.start and project.end. 
```{r}
splitdate = strsplit(trimws(grants1975$project.period), split = "THRU")
grants1975$project.start = sapply(splitdate, `[`, 1)
grants1975$project.end = sapply(splitdate, `[`, 2)
```

with these 2 new date columns, we clean them just like we cleaned the previous date columns. No date listed is marked with an ---, whereas an empty cell is given X
```{r}
grants1975$project.start = trimws(grants1975$project.start)
cleaned = gsub("\\s+", "", grants1975$project.start)
grants1975$project.start[grants1975$project.start == ""] = NA
dash_only = grepl("^-+$", cleaned)
parsed = sapply(grants1975$project.start, clean_date)
parsed = as.Date(parsed, origin = "1970-01-01")
grants1975$project.start_clean = format(parsed, "%m-%d-%y")
grants1975$project.start_clean[dash_only] = "---"
grants1975$project.start_clean[is.na(grants1975$project.start_clean)] = "X"
```

```{r}
grants1975[, c("project.start", "project.start_clean")]
```


For award amount, some cells have $ while others do not. For all cells, i am removing \$ so they can easily be formatted in excel later in time. I also found some had a D instead of an \$. I also adjust this. Some cells are a little more difficult in that some values are not picking up (ex: ,050,000 is a cell but there are numbers before).i mark these values with a Y
```{r}
grants1975$award.amount = trimws(grants1975$award.amount)
flagged_vals = grepl("^[,0]", grants1975$award.amount)
grants1975$award.amount[flagged_vals] = "Y"
grants1975$award.amount[grants1975$award.amount != "Y"] = gsub("\\$", "", grants1975$award.amount[grants1975$award.amount != "Y"])
grants1975$award.amount[grants1975$award.amount != "Y"] = gsub(",", "", grants1975$award.amount[grants1975$award.amount != "Y"])
grants1975$award.amount[grants1975$award.amount != "Y"] = gsub("\\.", "", grants1975$award.amount[grants1975$award.amount != "Y"])
grants1975$award.amount[grants1975$award.amount != "Y"] = gsub("[A-Za-z]+", "", grants1975$award.amount[grants1975$award.amount != "Y"])
numpart = as.numeric(grants1975$award.amount[grants1975$award.amount != "Y"])
grants1975$award.amount[grants1975$award.amount != "Y"] = as.character(numpart)
grants1975$award.amount[is.na(grants1975$award.amount)] = "X"
```
a few results to observe that my cleaning was successful
```{r}
sort(table(grants1975$award.amount), decreasing = TRUE)
```

```{r}
grants1975$eligible.cost[grants1975$eligible.cost != "Y"] = gsub("\\$", "", grants1975$eligible.cost[grants1975$eligible.cost != "Y"])
grants1975$eligible.cost[grants1975$eligible.cost != "Y"] = gsub(",", "", grants1975$eligible.cost[grants1975$eligible.cost != "Y"])
grants1975$eligible.cost[grants1975$eligible.cost != "Y"] = gsub("\\.", "", grants1975$eligible.cost[grants1975$eligible.cost != "Y"])
grants1975$eligible.cost[grants1975$eligible.cost != "Y"] = gsub("[A-Za-z]+", "", grants1975$eligible.cost[grants1975$eligible.cost != "Y"])
numpart = as.numeric(grants1975$eligible.cost[grants1975$eligible.cost != "Y"])
```

award amount should be about 75% of eligible cost. we check this below. If this is not fulfilled then award amount is flagged with checkval, since either award amount or eligible cost can have the error. this also flags if award amount is greater than eligible cost; this shouldn't be possible, so if this is the case, it is also flagged with checkval

```{r}
grants1975$award.amount.num = as.numeric(gsub("[^0-9.-]", "", grants1975$award.amount))
grants1975$eligible.cost.num = as.numeric(gsub("[^0-9.-]", "", grants1975$eligible.cost))

grants1975$award.amount_clean = grants1975$award.amount.num
x_num = suppressWarnings(as.numeric(grants1975$award.amount.num))
y_num = suppressWarnings(as.numeric(grants1975$eligible.cost.num))

numeric_rows = !is.na(x_num) & !is.na(y_num)

grants1975$award.amount_clean[
  numeric_rows & (x_num < 0.70 * y_num | x_num > y_num)
] = NA
grants1975$award.amount_clean[is.na(grants1975$award.amount_clean)] = paste0("checkvals_", grants1975$award.amount.num[is.na(grants1975$award.amount_clean)])
```

we observe our results below. my new values are in the award.amount_clean column
```{r}
grants1975[, c("award.amount.num", "award.amount_clean", "eligible.cost.num")]
```

our cleaning was successful, so we override the old column with my new column
```{r}
grants1975$award.amount = grants1975$award.amount_clean
grants1975 = grants1975 %>%  select(-c(award.amount_clean, award.amount.num, eligible.cost.num))
```

```{r}
)

grants1975$level.of.treatment_clean <- valid_levels[
  amatch(grants1975$level.of.treatment, valid_levels, method = "jw", maxDist = 0.20)
]

table(grants1975$level.of.treatment_clean, useNA = "always")
grants1975$level.of.treatment_clean[is.na(grants1975$level.of.treatment_clean)] = paste0("incorrect_", grants1975$level.of.treatment[is.na(grants1975$level.of.treatment_clean)])
```

these edits take place after going through the cleaned excel file and filling in all entries for state. we now validate the entries obtained in the city column. we do this through verifying the city in the original city column is part of the state it is in. if it isn't, it is marked as incorrect. if it is, it is left the same
```{r}
tempdf = read.csv("1975progress2 - Sheet 1.csv", header = TRUE)
```

```{r}
tempdf$city_clean <- toupper(trimws(tempdf$city))
tempdf$state_clean <- toupper(trimws(tempdf$state))
tempdf$city_clean[tempdf$city_clean == ""] <- "X"
tempdf$state_validation <- tempdf$state_clean
tempdf$state_validation[
  tempdf$state_validation == "NB"
] <- "NE"

city_state_ref <- unique(
  rbind(
    data.frame(
      city = toupper(trimws(zip_code_db$major_city)),
      state = toupper(trimws(zip_code_db$state))
    ),
    data.frame(
      city = toupper(trimws(zip_code_db$post_office_city)),
      state = toupper(trimws(zip_code_db$state))
    )
  )
)

city_state_ref <- city_state_ref[
  !is.na(city_state_ref$city) &
    city_state_ref$city != "",
]



valid_pair <- paste(
  tempdf$city_clean,
  tempdf$state_validation
) %in% paste(
  city_state_ref$city,
  city_state_ref$state
)


tempdf$city_clean[
  !valid_pair &
  tempdf$city_clean != "X"
] <- paste0(
  "incorrect_",
  tempdf$city[
    !valid_pair &
    tempdf$city_clean != "X"
  ]
)

tempdf$state_validation <- NULL
```

```{r}
tempdf[, c("city", "city_clean")]
```


```{r}
tempdf$city = tempdf$city_clean
tempdf = tempdf %>%  select(-c(city_clean, state_clean))
```

